assumptions_for_gate_3: A1 (E3, planner's inference; the architect confirms or overturns at Gate 3). The stored per-person choice is a client node id and nothing else, read literally from BR3 ('a node id rather than a client name') and BR17 ('the stored per-person choice is a client'). Choosing 'All' is therefore a session state and is not stored: a person who chooses All and returns opens on their last stored client, or on nothing chosen if they never stored one. The alternative, a reserved 'All' token in the map so a person who prefers All is restored to it, is one extra branch in the step 13 arm and the step 16 seed; it is not built here because no rule in ART-20260905-023 asks for it and BR16 calls nothing chosen a first-use state without saying All ends it. If the product owner meant All to be remembered, the specification needs a version 7 before step 13 is built; the plan changes in two places.

A2 (E3, planner's reading of BR9, BR10, BR12 and BR18 together). Scoping is applied uniformly: for every internal seat, exempt or not, the rows under All and under an explicit client are the person's stakeholder projects plus records with no project-tier ancestor (BR9, BR10, BR12), and the dropdown lists the clients of exactly those rows (BR9). BR12's 'any client remains choosable' and BR18's 'ability to choose any client explicitly is unchanged' are read as: no choice is refused and no access changes, while what an explicit choice LISTS is governed by BR10. Under this reading an exempt seat that is a member of no project lists only ungated records whatever it chooses, which is what BR18's first sentence says ('see nothing under All until made members'). The other reading, that an explicit choice by an exempt seat lists that client's whole payload, contradicts BR10's second sentence ('scoping is a property of the person's view, not of the All option') and is not built. If the product owner meant the other reading, the specification needs a version 7 and step 6's explicit-client branch changes; nothing else moves.

A3 (E3). With a stored choice restored, the Filters chip counts that client as one active filter, because it is one; AC1's rule that the chip does not count the resting value concerns the sentinel only. Nothing in the specification says otherwise; recorded so it is not mistaken for an omission.

A4 (E1, read from lib/db/persist.ts:938-949 on the branch). The persistence switch writes the operating-model document only for the action kinds it names (setNotificationPref, upsertSavedView, deleteSavedView, config); a new model-writing kind that is not added there is applied in memory and lost on reload. lib/db/persist.ts is therefore in the preference-storage workstream and step 13 touches it. It is not a protected path in .claude/contracts/registry.json.

body.rollback: Revert the commits in reverse order; no schema change. Version 2 named step 1 (now step 1) the highest regression risk and it is built; of the remaining steps, step 6 is the highest because every row list in the workspace passes through matchesFilters, visibleRows and facetsOf, and a scope test with the wrong polarity hides every member's work or shows every non-member's — CD4 is the guard, and the optional parameter means a revert of step 15 alone restores today's unscoped behaviour without touching step 6. Four cautions. (1) Reverting the step 15 commit restores unscoped All for exempt seats and the 'All clients' report header; non-exempt seats are unaffected because the read gate never stopped narrowing their payload. (2) Reverting the step 13/14 commit removes the arm, the shape, the kind, the permission row, the clientView withholding and the persist case; a clientChoices key already written into a tenant's OperatingModel JSON rides along after the revert because mergeModel spreads stored wholesale (lib/config.ts:1609), and a reverted clientView no longer withholds it from client seats — so a rollback of step 13 after any tenant has written must also strip the key from each tenant's OperatingModel row, or the revert lands before any write. Steps 16 and 17 must be reverted first or the UI dispatches a kind the route refuses. (3) Reverting the step 11/12 commit restores the browser-only guard of 961c14e only if step 17 is reverted with it; reverting step 11 alone leaves step 17's applySavedFilters import dangling, so the order is 17, 16, 15, 13/14, 11/12, 9/10, 6/7/8. (4) A saved view stored at the canonical resting value by step 11 loads under a reverted parseSavedFilters as the sentinel through the spread of EMPTY_FILTERS and applies an empty grid — fail-closed, and the same state the low finding of ART-20260905-019 describes, not a data loss.
